literalGroups.primaryGround: The exact retained Merriam-Webster shirt sense 1a describes a cloth upper-body garment usually with a collar, sleeves, a front opening and a tail long enough to tuck into trousers or a skirt (L40-L45). The prompt is explicitly anchored to that dictionary definition and does not require a button closure, a full-length opening, or any inference that a polo cannot have a short placket. The polo distractor was removed and replaced with blouse, whose usual entry is a loose-fitting neck-to-waist garment (L58). The remaining familiar garments have distinct usual dictionary descriptions.
